props.gloss_en: R' Eliezer: one who slits the ear of a firstborn may never slaughter it
the Sages: if another blemish develops in it, he may slaughter it on that one
one who had a baheret and it was [unintentionally] excised -- he is pure
excised it intentionally -- R' Eliezer: when another mark develops on him he will be purified from it
the Sages: [not] until it spreads over all of him, or until his baheret shrinks below a split bean
Rabba and Rav Yosef: when R' Eliezer penalizes, it is in his property; in his body he does not penalize
[regarding] his property one can say he will come to do it; his body -- can one say he will come to do it?

Rava: in both the Rabbis penalized him in what he did -- he meant to permit it by this blemish, so they penalized him in this blemish; he meant to purify himself by this excision, so they penalized him in this excision
[R' Eliezer's word in Nega'im 7:5] was taught 'yit'har'
[R' Eliezer's word] was taught 'veyit'har'
what is the practical difference? a bridegroom on whom a mark appeared
a bridegroom on whom a mark appeared -- they give him seven days, for him, his cloak and his garment; and likewise on a festival -- all the days of the festival
if you say 'yit'har' -- he is purified of the first, and for the latter they wait for him the seven feast days
if you say 'veyit'har' -- in the end, though he is not made impure by the latter, he stands impure from the first
one who sold his slave to gentiles and died -- they penalized his son after him, since every single day he removes him from mitzvot
one who timed his work for the intermediate festival days and died -- they did not penalize his son after him, since he did not do it in prohibition
the Rabbis penalized him, and he is no longer [here]
or perhaps the Rabbis penalized his property, and it is [still] here
a field cleared of thorns in the Sabbatical year may be sown after it; improved [or] fenced for manure -- it may not be sown after the Sabbatical year
Rav Asi b' R' Chanina: we hold -- he improved it and died, his son sows it
R' Zeira: evidently the Rabbis penalized him; his son the Rabbis did not penalize
Abaye: we hold -- one who defiled [another's] taharot and died, they did not penalize his son after him
what is the reason? damage that is not noticeable is not damage; [it is] a rabbinic fine -- him the Rabbis penalized, his son they did not

questions.gloss_en: Rav Pappa: did we learn 'yit'har' or 'veyit'har' [in R' Eliezer's statement]? -- the difference is the bridegroom's seven days; unresolved, teiku
